Periodic trigonometric functions become invertible only after restricting their domains. The chosen restricted ranges define the principal inverse values.
The reverse compositions return the original angle only when it lies in the relevant principal range.

items.text: Real arcsine and arccosine inputs lie in [-1,1]; real arctangent accepts every real input.
Solving a trigonometric equation requires adding periodic families after finding principal reference values.

runs.text: Because 3pi/4 is outside the principal arcsine range,
The inverse returns the angle in [-pi/2, pi/2] having the same sine.

items.text: Inverse notation does not mean reciprocal notation.
Do not cancel a trigonometric function with its inverse in the reverse order without checking the principal range.
A principal inverse value is one representative, not the complete solution set of a periodic equation.
